subject: Clarify delivery commitments for live vs polled endpoints — exception & plan
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@clearsky-analytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Delivery commitments for live vs polled endpoints — need clarification

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from our engineering/product teams after the POC: we need explicit commitments for two different modes: a) live streaming (token-by-token) used in our transcription/live-assist flows and b) polled/batched endpoints used for large-batch post-processing. The key asks are:

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectation for streaming (typical utterance lengths are ~8–30 tokens). UX dropoff if first token > 700ms.
- Sustained tokens/sec expectation for long responses (100–200+ tokens) so the UI remains interactive.
- Clear failure/fallback behavior: if streaming degrades, do we fall back to polling? How does billing and SLA differ?

We want to include an exception in the SOW if the streaming TTFT SLO cannot be met across public hosted regions — we can consider Dedicated capacity but need a clear operational plan.

Attached is a small sample of traces from our POC (latency-metrics-capture.csv). Can you propose the minimal commitments Redwood can make and an acceptance test we can run?

Thanks,
Maria
Product Lead, ClearSky Analytics
[attachment: latency-metrics-capture.csv (text/csv)]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@clearsky-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery commitments for live vs polled endpoints — need clarification

Hi Maria — thanks for the traces, that's helpful. Quick responses and a proposed next step:

Short answers:
- TTFT (streaming): we can target median TTFT <= 200ms on Redwood-hosted endpoints under the POC traffic profile, with a 95th percentile carveout at 850ms for public-hosted regions.
- Sustained outgoing token rate: for streaming we recommend a conservative baseline of 40 tokens/sec per connection for shared-hosted; Dedicated GPU pools can guarantee 150+ tokens/sec depending on model/quantization.
- Fallbacks: our standard approach is automated routing: when streaming availability or TTFT SLO breaches are detected, we can failover to a polled endpoint (synchronous batch) with an SLA note — polling provides higher sustained throughput but increased initial latency. Billing follows consumed tokens; we can discuss credits for SLA violations.

Attachments: I attached a draft SOW and a short runbook we use when negotiating carveouts. Can you confirm expected peak concurrency and whether you can run the Redwood synthetic acceptance harness during a staging window? That lets us baseline TTFT and tokens/sec on your traffic distribution.

Proposing a working session tomorrow 10 am PT to align on acceptance tests. I'll loop in Aditya (runtime) and Soojin (SRE) on recommended measurement windows.

—Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
[attachment: SOW_streaming_vs_polling_draft.pdf (application/pdf)]
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Delivery commitments for live vs polled endpoints — measurement & carveouts (internal)

Internal notes / recommended conservative commitments before legal/Sales finalizes:

- Measurement methodology: run 3 x 30-minute windows across hours of day (low/mid/high) with a synthetic harness that mirrors ClearSky packet sizes and sequence length distribution. TTFT = time from request acceptance -> emission of first byte. Use p50/p95/p99 windows.
- Proposed guardrails (public-hosted):
  * Streaming TTFT: p50 <= 220ms, p95 <= 900ms (we include 95th percentile carveout for multi-region variability).
  * Streaming sustained rate (shared-hosted): baseline guarantee = 40 tokens/sec sustained over 60s; recommended Dedicated offer for 100+ tokens/sec sustained.
  * Polling endpoints (sync): p50 start-to-first-byte <= 400ms for short requests, but for large batch we treat throughput not TTFT.
- Exception control plane: if public-hosted p95 breaches occur > 3x in a rolling 7-day window under the agreed harness, Redwood triggers an operational remediation and offers either a temporary credit or migration to a Dedicated pool (customer choice).

Operational ask: require ClearSky to run the harness in staging for 48 hours and share logs. We should also include a canary rollout (5–10% traffic) before cutting over.

I'll draft the carveout language for SOW and the acceptance test steps.

-Soojin
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@clearsky-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery commitments for live vs polled endpoints — need clarification

Maria — following internal alignment, here is a succinct proposal you can review and sign off (we'll fold into the SOW):

1) Baseline commitments (Public-hosted endpoints, POC traffic):
   - Streaming TTFT: p50 <= 220ms; p95 <= 900ms.
   - Streaming sustained token throughput (shared-hosted): baseline guarantee of 40 tokens/sec per connection measured over 60s windows; sustained bursts subject to capacity.
   - Polling (sync) endpoints: p50 start <= 400ms for small requests; bulk batch throughput measured as tokens/minute with no TTFT guarantee.

2) Exception / remedial path:
   - Acceptance test: ClearSky runs Redwood synthetic harness in staging for 48 hours (3 x 30-min windows representative of traffic). Labs to provide logs and sample traces.
   - If p95 breaches occur >3 times in a rolling 7-day window under the agreed harness, Redwood will:
       a) Prioritize traffic to Dedicated capacity if available (migration plan included); or
       b) Offer a proportional credit for tokens affected while we remediate.
   - Billing: normal token billing applies; credits only for verified SLA breaches under acceptance harness.

3) Dedicated offer (optional):
   - For customers that require interactive long-form streaming (>=100 tokens/sec sustained), Redwood recommends Dedicated GPU pool; we can provide sizing guidance following their 48-hour harness run. Dedicated pools have tighter TTFT and throughput commitments and a defined migration window (3 business days).

Next steps: if you agree in principle I will have Legal draft the SOW carveout language and the PO path. Can you confirm you can run the harness starting Thursday 19 Jun?

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@clearsky-analytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Delivery commitments for live vs polled endpoints — SOW carveout (final)

Hi Maria / team — legal here. Per Karthik and Soojin, we've drafted the carveout clause to include the measurement windows, p50/p95 targets for streaming, the remedial migration path to Dedicated, and the credit calculation methodology. Highlights:

- Measurement windows and harness definition will be appended as Exhibit A (technical acceptance tests).
- SLA breach credit: proportional to token consumption in affected windows; credit escalates if remediation timeline exceeds 5 business days.
- Dedicated migration: Redwood will provide Dedicated capacity estimates within 48 hours of validated harness logs and coordinate a 3-business-day migration plan upon PO and capacity confirmation.

Please confirm acceptance of the above and provide the PO reference for deal CLSK-2025-0701 so we can finalize SOW and signature. If you prefer, sign the attached redline and we'll incorporate.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
